title: Copying a suffix from an interior position
statement: Let $M$ be a machine with no work tapes over the Boolean alphabet, and let $q$ be a state. Suppose that for every input symbol and work-tape tuple, in state $q$ the transition on a bit $b$ moves right, emits $b$, and returns to $q$, while on blank it stays in place, emits nothing, and halts. For finite Boolean strings $x,\mathrm{rest},o$ and a natural number $\mathrm{pre}$ such that $x=\mathrm{pre}++\mathrm{rest}$, after $|\mathrm{rest}|+1$ steps from the scan configuration at position $|\mathrm{pre}|$ in state $q$ with output $o$, the machine is in the halted scan configuration at position $|x|$ with output $o$ followed by $\mathrm{rest}$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ has no work tapes, uses the Boolean alphabet, and has state set containing $q$
For every input symbol and work-tape tuple, on a scanned bit $b$ the transition moves right, emits $b$, and returns to $q$

replaced:
Suppose a control state $q$ of a machine without work tapes emits each scanned
bit and moves right, and halts silently on the blank. If $x = p s$ is a split
of the input into a prefix $p$ and suffix $s$, then $\abs{s}+1$ steps from the
scan configuration at position $\abs{p}$ in state $q$ with prior output $o$
reach a halted configuration with output $o$ followed by $s$.
